steps.name: Case Initiation
steps.description: Open an investigation case when an exposure exception is received; record the portfolio, security or issuer, reported exposure, applicable threshold, and alert generation time. Treat the alert as a trigger, not a final breach determination.

steps.name: Mandate Retrieval
steps.description: Retrieve the investment mandate governing the portfolio and identify the restriction associated with the alert, reviewing narrative provisions, schedules, definitions, and supporting documents in context.

steps.name: Position Evidence
steps.description: Obtain the holdings snapshot used to generate the alert and, where necessary, retrieve intraday position information to establish the portfolio's exposure at relevant points in time and verify the reported value.

steps.name: Transaction History Review
steps.description: Review historical transactions (purchases, sales, transfers, other activity) affecting the security or issuer to determine whether the exposure changed due to an active decision or another event, comparing transaction timestamps with the exposure change where available.

steps.name: Exception and Waiver Search
steps.description: Check for pre-approved exceptions, temporary waivers, or other documented permissions that may have applied at the time of the alert, verifying the validity and effective period of any approval identified.

steps.name: Corporate Actions and Passive Movement Analysis
steps.description: Assess whether a corporate action, market movement, or other event could have changed the exposure without an active investment decision, comparing available evidence.

steps.name: Root-Cause Assessment
steps.description: Synthesize the evidence to determine the most plausible cause (active investment decision, passive market drift, corporate action, operational issue, or other documented circumstance); record uncertainty and escalate where evidence is conflicting or incomplete.

steps.name: Genuine Breach or False Positive Classification
steps.description: Classify the alert as a genuine breach (mandate restriction actually violated) or a false positive (allowable circumstance, data issue, or other condition) based on mandate language, position data, transaction history, and applicable approvals.

steps.name: Compliance Write-Up
steps.description: Prepare a written investigation summary covering the original alert, relevant mandate provisions, evidence reviewed, root-cause assessment, applicable exceptions or approvals, final classification, and recommended action.

steps.name: Escalation and Human Oversight
steps.description: Escalate material cases, uncertain interpretations, and incomplete-evidence situations to compliance or investment oversight personnel; the final compliance determination remains subject to the firm's established governance process.

steps.name: Case Initiation
steps.description: Open a new investigation case when an exposure exception is received. Record the portfolio, security or issuer involved, the reported exposure, the applicable threshold, and the time the alert was generated. Treat the initial alert as an investigation trigger rather than a final breach determination.

steps.name: Mandate Retrieval
steps.description: Retrieve the investment mandate governing the portfolio and identify the restriction associated with the alert. Review relevant language in narrative provisions, schedules, definitions, or supporting documents in context, since a numerical alert may not capture every qualification affecting how the mandate applies.

steps.name: Position Evidence
steps.description: Obtain the holdings snapshot used to generate the alert and, where necessary, retrieve intraday position information surrounding the reported breach. Establish the portfolio's exposure at relevant points in time and determine whether the reported value accurately reflects the position during the period under investigation.

steps.name: Transaction History Review
steps.description: Review historical transactions affecting the relevant security or issuer, including purchases, sales, transfers, and other recorded activity, to determine whether the exposure changed due to an active portfolio decision or another event. Compare transaction timestamps with the timing of the exposure change where available.

steps.name: Exception and Waiver Search
steps.description: Check for pre-approved exceptions, temporary waivers, or other documented permissions that may have applied at the time of the alert. These records may be maintained separately from portfolio data in documents or case-management records. Verify the validity and effective period of any approval identified.

steps.name: Corporate Actions and Passive Movement Analysis
steps.description: Consider whether a corporate action, market movement, or other event could have changed the exposure without a corresponding active investment decision, such as a market-value change pushing an exposure percentage above a threshold without a new purchase. Compare the available evidence before reaching a conclusion.

steps.name: Root-Cause Assessment
steps.description: Synthesize the evidence to determine the most plausible cause of the exception, classifying it as an active investment decision, passive market drift, corporate action, operational issue, or another documented circumstance. Where evidence is conflicting or incomplete, record the uncertainty and follow the applicable escalation procedure rather than treating an assumption as fact.

steps.name: Genuine Breach or False Positive Classification
steps.description: After considering the mandate language, position data, transaction history, and applicable approvals, classify the alert. Record a genuine breach where evidence supports that the mandate restriction was actually violated; record a false positive where the alert resulted from an allowable circumstance, data issue, or other condition meaning the apparent breach is not a reportable violation.

steps.name: Compliance Write-Up
steps.description: Prepare a written investigation summary describing the original alert, relevant mandate provisions, evidence reviewed, root-cause assessment, applicable exceptions or approvals, final classification, and recommended action, so another reviewer can understand how the conclusion was reached without reconstructing the investigation from source systems.

steps.name: Escalation and Human Oversight
steps.description: Escalate material cases, uncertain interpretations, and situations involving incomplete evidence to the appropriate compliance or investment oversight personnel. The final regulatory or compliance determination remains subject to the firm's established governance process, and authorized personnel retain responsibility for approving sensitive conclusions.
